answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using hardware-rooted remote attestation. Agents must generate cryptographic proofs within secure enclaves timed by a physical crystal oscillator, forcing an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of procuring dedicated silicon per persona. Protocols filter admissions through a jade verifier and organize active nodes into a lotus topology. However, microarchitectural side-channel attacks and reliance on centralized vendor keys undermine trust.
